baseline.reason: Built and ran pre_intro (7099b09e9629), post_intro (771449f14a35) and post_benign (7099b09e9629 + fix) in Docker with the project's ASan+UBSan build. The freetype fuzzer harness's fixed pixel sizes (16/72) never reach the vulnerable code with enough magnitude, and the bug also requires (a) the target glyph's codepoint to be in the autofit "tilde correction" adjustment database (only U+0168/U+0169 qualify), (b) the font to supply usable "blue zone" reference glyphs (else the whole Latin autofit style is disabled), and (c) every one of the ~130 adjustment-database codepoints to resolve via cmap (otherwise an unrelated pre-existing OOB in af_reverse_character_map_new fires first) — none of which the stock harness or its default sizes provide, so no existing/default PoC could reach it. I reverse-engineered af_latin_stretch_tilde's exact wiggle-detection condition (an on-curve point flanked by two off-curve control points sharing its y, both further on-curve neighbors on the same side) from source, and hand-built a minimal SFNT font plus a small custom FT harness (compiled and run against the library under test with the same sanitizer flags as the canonical build) to drive height=max_y-min_y to ~6.19e9 and target_height within 64 units of it. Same font/command across all three builds: pre_intro exits cleanly (0, no crash), post_intro aborts (exit 134) with 'UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: undefined-behavior /work/src/autofit/aflatin.c:3035:34 ... signed integer overflow: 1490304752 * 6192402018 cannot be represented in type long' inside af_latin_stretch_tilde <- af_latin_hints_apply <- af_autofitter_load_glyph, exactly matching the labelled root cause and the oss-fuzz crash state (af_latin_stretch_bottom_tilde/af_latin_hints_apply/af_autofitter_load_glyph); post_benign (fix applied) again exits cleanly (0, no crash). This cleanly confirms introduction by the intro commit and remediation by the benign/fix commit.
